result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.
result.answer:
I found two work orders on Transformer 1. Both need the unit de-energized, but neither has a scheduled date, so under your 14-day rule I can'tform a bundle. High acetylene makes the OLTC inspection urgent, and I recommend doing both in one outage on **2026-10-01**.

**Work orders (both pending approval; there are no other open ones)**

| WO | Description | Priority | Scheduled date | Needs outage? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | None set. The notes give a target of 2024-01-19, which has passed. | **Yes.** The tap changer must be opened up. |
| 1000052 | Oilsample retest (DGA) and insulation check – thermal fault | 3 | None set. The notes give a target of 2026-10-01. | **Yes, in part.** The oil sample and furan test can be done live. The insulation resistance and power factor tests need the unit de-energized. |

**Bundling:** You have two outage-needing work orders, but a bundle needs two scheduled dates within 14 days of each other. Neither has a scheduled date, and the target dates in the notes are about 2.7 years apart. So no bundle meets the rule.

**Planned hours:** I can't estimate these. Neither work order has planned hours, and Transformer 1 has no closed work orders to average actual hours from.

**Latest gas readings (2024-01-19, about 2.7 years old):** Acetylene is **7 ppm**, above your 1 ppm trigger. Hydrogen is **2,850 ppm**, which is very high. Methane is 7,400 ppm and ethylene is 16,650 ppm. The oil temperature alarm and trip flags were also set on that reading. Since acetylene is above 1 ppm, the OLTC work moves to the earliest possible date.

**Recommendations**
- **1000051 (OLTC inspection): do it as soon as possible, not deferred.** Take the outage on **2026-10-01**, the earliest available date. The MAIN calendar has no other work scheduled from 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-31, so calendar load isn't a constraint. It is priority 1, it's past its target, and the acetylene points to arcing or contact coking.
- **1000052 (DGA retest and insulation check): do it in the same outage on 2026-10-01, not deferred.** Its target date is that day,so this is one outage instead of two, and it meets your preference even though it isn't a formal bundle. Take the oil sample while the unit is still live before the outage, so the DGA reflects normal operation. Then do the insulation resistance and power factor tests while it's de-energized. Deferring would leave a thermal fault near 700 °C untested next to a suspect tap changer.
- **Before 2026-10-01:** Both work orders are still awaiting approval and have no technician or planned hours. They need approval, a scheduled date, a technician and an hours estimate. Given how old the gas readings are, a fresh DGA would also confirm how urgent this is. I haven't changed any work orders.

However, it skipped several expected steps: it never called wo.get_workorder or wo.get_workorder_tasks to confirm scope beyond the list output, and it did not call wo.get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned (or a status=CLOSED filtered list) to explicitly verify the fallback-hours claim that Transformer 1 has no closed work orders, instead inferring it from the unfiltered list (total=2).
